## Summary

UK public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants last year, representing a 62% increase compared to 2019-20 levels. Despite the end of the pandemic, consultant spending has not returned to pre-Covid figures. This presents a significant challenge for the Starmer government, which has pledged to cut consultant spending in half during its term.

Recent developments include KPMG securing a contract worth up to £223m to train civil servants. Since Labour took office, approximately £650m in new consultant contracts have been awarded, though many were agreed before the government transition.

Labour peer and finance academic Prem Sikka criticized the situation, describing it as "scandalous" and arguing that a "cult of hiring consultants" has developed. He questioned the value consultants provide, suggesting they cannot meaningfully understand complex organizations in just a few weeks.
